name: Early Blight of Tomato
description: A common fungal disease of tomato characterized by dark concentric ring lesions on older leaves. It can also infect stems and fruit, causing defoliation and reducing fruit yield and quality.
symptoms: Small brown to black spots on older leaves with concentric rings (target-like)
Spots enlarging and coalescing causing leaf death
Stem lesions as dark sunken cankers at the base
Fruit lesions near the calyx as dark sunken spots with concentric ridges
causes: Extended leaf wetness from rain, dew, or overhead irrigation
Fungal survival on infected crop debris
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb preventively
Spray azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin at first symptoms
Use copper-based fungicides for organic production
Remove infected lower leaves to reduce inoculum
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant tomato varieties
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Space plants adequately for air circulation
Use drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
